clue.text: A little drink to keep the police sweet

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so the drink phrase goes round the police

parts.note: a drop is a little drink, so this gives A DROP
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: A small tipple offered to stay on the right side of the local constabulary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' signals the container. An acid drop is a sharp-tasting boiled sweet popular in Britain; CID is the British detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid drop is a tangy boiled confection, so it is one kind of sweet.

clue.text: Twice caught on the hop — and quickly

indicators.note: twice says the piece built from the next words is written two times over

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
taken as written from the clue

explanation.surface: Someone caught off guard twice, urged to hurry up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twice' doubles C + HOP; 'on the' and 'and' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled phrase is an informal urging to hurry, so it is an adverbial way of saying fast.

clue.text: Style of expression out of play originally in Latin, for example

indicators.note: originally says this piece comes at the start, ahead of the other part

parts.note: a ball out of play is dead in many ball games
language can mean a style or manner of expression, as in flowery language

explanation.surface: A turn of phrase taken out of a stage play that first came from Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' sets the out-of-play piece at the front. 'play' suggests drama, but it is the sporting sense: a dead ball is out of play.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin is no longer anyone's first spoken tongue, the standard example of an extinct speech.

clue.text: Aromatic tender duck left to cook

indicators.note: to cook something is to work it over, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so it gives the letter O

explanation.surface: A fragrant, tender duck set aside to roast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cook' rearranges TENDER + O + L into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Redolent means strongly smelling or fragrant, a close synonym of aromatic.

clue.text: Time-consuming business makes friend swear

parts.note: a pal is a friend
to aver is to declare firmly, to swear something is true

explanation.surface: A drawn-out chore that drives a mate to curse.
explanation.definitionFit: A palaver is a fuss or tedious rigmarole, which is a time-consuming business.

clue.text: Group of languages more oblique than Roman

definitions.meaning: the ... branch of Indo-European includes Latin and its relatives
... type slants, while roman type stands upright

explanation.definitionFit: Italic names both a language family of ancient Italy and a sloping typeface, contrasted with upright roman type.

clue.text: Listened to drug report

indicators.note: listened to signals that the word is taken by its sound rather than spelling

parts.note: bhang is a cannabis preparation from India

explanation.surface: Someone heard about a drug in a news report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listened to' says BHANG, the drug, is heard, giving the same sound written without the H.
explanation.definitionFit: A bang is a loud noise, and report means the sharp sound of a gunshot.

clue.text: Contract to remove wrinkles

definitions.meaning: to contract is to shrink or lessen

explanation.definitionFit: Decrease means to reduce or shrink, and split playfully it means taking out creases.

clue.text: Mechanise co-driver?

definitions.meaning: to mechanise a process is to make it run by machine
read whimsically as a car's partner: an auto's mate

explanation.definitionFit: To automate is to make machines do work; split, it reads as a motor car's companion.

clue.text: Star and famous lover half falling out

indicators.note: half falling out says the first half of the lover's name drops away

parts.note: Casanova was the notorious eighteenth-century Venetian seducer

explanation.surface: A celebrity and a renowned lover, half of whom are quarrelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half falling out' removes CASA from CASANOVA. 'falling out' suggests a quarrel, but it means letters dropping off.
explanation.definitionFit: A nova is a star that suddenly flares up in brightness.

clue.text: Blunder in regal PR can do damage

indicators.note: damage means the letters are knocked out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A royal publicity blunder that public relations could make worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damage' rearranges REGALPRCANDO; 'do' is part of the fodder, not a verb with 'damage'.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop a clanger is a British idiom for making an embarrassing mistake.

clue.text: Original speech from evening out at reunion

indicators.note: a reunion brings parts back together in a new way, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Old dialect heard again at a night out at a reunion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reunion' rearranges EVENINGOUTAT.
explanation.definitionFit: One's native tongue is the first language one learns, the original speech of a person.

clue.text: Expression heard in fights …

indicators.note: heard says the word is taken by its sound alone

parts.note: frays are brawls or fights

explanation.surface: Words spoken during brawls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' gives the sound of FRAYS, spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase is a group of words, a verbal expression.

clue.text: … and so on, usually shortened

parts.note: the Latin tag for and so on is normally written as a three-letter abbreviation with a point

explanation.surface: Continuing the list, as people tend to abbreviate it.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses link this clue to the previous one in the surface reading only.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means and the rest, usually written abbreviated as etc.

clue.text: Drinkers admitting greedy chap's given bungs

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: sots are habitual drunkards
a pig is a greedy person; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: Drunks letting a glutton in, and the glutton handed bribes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' signals the container. 'bungs' looks like bribes (British slang) but means stoppers.
explanation.definitionFit: A spigot is a peg or plug for the vent of a cask, a kind of bung.

clue.text: Introduction to explanation, initially in small capitals?

definitions.text: Introduction to explanation, initially in small capitals?

parts.words: Introduction to explanation, initially in small capitals?
parts.note: the Latin word for namely introduces a clarification and is abbreviated as sc, which also stands for small capitals

explanation.surface: A preface to an explanation, perhaps set in small capitals.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin word for 'namely' is abbreviated sc., the same letters printers use for small capitals.
explanation.definitionFit: Scilicet means namely or that is to say, a word that leads into an explanation.

clue.text: Soldier may be retiring

definitions.meaning: the lowest rank in the army
retiring means shy or reserved, keeping to oneself

explanation.definitionFit: A private is a soldier of the lowest rank, and as an adjective it means withdrawn or secluded.

clue.text: Change direction again and enter Rio in a storm

indicators.note: in a storm suggests wild disorder, so the letters are churned up

explanation.surface: Turning back to come into Rio during a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a storm' rearranges ENTERRIO; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To reorient is to turn to face a new way again, changing direction once more.

clue.text: Go and pelt rat

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a go at a game
a pelt is an animal's coat

explanation.surface: An instruction to go and throw things at a rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pelt' and 'rat' read as attacking a rodent; 'rat' means a traitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is slang for a deserter or betrayer, and a turncoat changes sides.

clue.text: Express in abstract English

parts.note: an abstract is a summary, a précis

explanation.surface: A request to put something into an English summary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' is the adjective, as in an express instruction, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Express as an adjective means explicit and exact, so it is a synonym of exact or definite.

clue.text: Corsican, for example, seen to end up in river, endlessly

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
endlessly means the river's last letter is cut off

parts.note: the Isère is a river in south-east France
to land somewhere is to end up there

explanation.surface: A man from Corsica spotted finishing up in a river with no end to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the river's final letter and 'in' signals the container; 'seen' is a link word. The Isère flows through the French Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsica is an island, so a Corsican is an example of an inhabitant of an island.

clue.text: Spoil rising boy model

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: Ed is a boy's name, short for Edward
a form is a model or pattern

explanation.surface: A youngster climbing up to ruin a model he made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns ED into DE in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To deform something is to mar its shape, spoiling it.

clue.text: Call for dismissal in uproar

parts.note: out is a batter's dismissal in cricket
a cry is a call

explanation.surface: A demand for someone's sacking amid a hubbub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' joins the pieces; the dismissal is the cricket sense, the umpire's out.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcry is a loud public protest, a clamour or uproar.

clue.text: Tense, approaching island without a flaw

indicators.note: without means outside, so the other pieces go round the island

parts.note: the imperfect is a past tense of continuing action
on can mean approaching, as in getting on for

explanation.surface: Nervously nearing an island that has no defect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, so the island letter sits within. It looks like 'lacking', which would point the opposite way.
explanation.definitionFit: An imperfection is a defect or blemish, so it means a fault.

clue.text: Cut off top voting returns

definitions.meaning: to ... a tree or animal is to remove its top or horns
the tally of votes cast at an election

explanation.definitionFit: Poll means to lop the head of a tree, and also an election count.

clue.text: Continue to appear someone rather stupid

definitions.meaning: to keep going or carry on
to come onstage as a performer

explanation.definitionFit: The two-word phrase means carry on or step onstage; joined up, it is slang for a fool.

clue.text: It shows title to book written in Latin

definitions.text: It shows title to book written in Latin

parts.words: It shows title to book written in Latin
parts.note: title is ownership, not a book's name: a label in a volume naming its owner, phrased in Latin

explanation.surface: Something displaying a book's name penned in the old Roman language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'title' suggests a book's name, but it means legal ownership.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means from the books of, printed on a bookplate stating who owns the volume.

clue.text: Appeal from opponents to come to terms with end of hostility

parts.note: in bridge, East and North sit as opponents, giving E and N
to treat is to negotiate an agreement

indicators.note: end of picks out the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A plea from enemies to settle terms once fighting ends.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are North, South, East and West; N and E are on opposing sides.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest request, a plea or appeal.
